suresh: Quick heads-up — ran a per-channel outlier scan as part of the quant bakeoff on gpt-ish-7b-v0. Found concentrated outlier channels in attn.q for layers 9-12 and a big spike in ffn.lin2 at layer 30. FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ all behave differently on these.

suresh: Command I used:
```
python tools/outlier_scan.py \\  --model models/gpt-ish-7b-v0 \\  --quant-modes fp8 int8 gptq awq \\  --threshold 3.0 \\  --per-channel --out /tmp/scan_gptish7b.json
```

anna: mind pasting the top offending channels? :eyes:

suresh: pasted the top findings (trimmed):
```
layer  | type   | channel | max_abs | outlier_ratio | suggested_action
9      | attn.q | 42      | 4.7     | 0.041         | gptq-fallback / channel-scale
10     | attn.q | 7       | 3.9     | 0.033         | channel-scale
11     | attn.q | 112     | 5.2     | 0.048         | skip-quantize / gptq
30     | ffn.lin2| 5      | 6.1     | 0.062         | skip-quantize (keep fp16)
34     | attn.k | 3       | 3.1     | 0.028         | channel-scale
```

elliot: From the bakeoff metrics: overall GPTQ -> lowest perplexity delta but MUCH slower conversion time; AWQ -> fastest but 0.8-1.4% accuracy regression concentrated on these outlier layers. INT8 native has inconsistent behavior depending on blocksize. FP8 looks promising on average, but spikes at those channels.

maya: proposal for a "layer rescue" policy we can bake into onboarding:
- if outlier_ratio >= 0.05 -> mark layer as "must-keep-fp16" (skip quantize)
- if 0.02 <= outlier_ratio < 0.05 -> attempt per-channel scaling then re-run quant simulation
- if per-channel scaling fails (delta > threshold) -> fallback to GPTQ for that layer only
- always record per-layer fallback in model profile for serving routing

maya: quick pseudo-config for rollout profile:
```json
{
  "quant_mode": "awq",
  "rescue_policy": {
    "outlier_ratio_keep_fp16": 0.05,
    "channel_scale_try": true,
    "gptq_fallback_enabled": true
  },
  "deploy_profile": {
    "hosted": {"default": "awq", "fallback": "gptq-layer-fallback"},
    "dedicated": {"default": "gptq", "force_fp16_layers": []}
  }
}
```

elliot: +1 to per-layer GPTQ fallback. Practically that means conversion pipeline needs to accept a per-layer override list instead of single global method. I can add that to the converter.

anna: any numbers on end-to-end eval after applying channel-scale vs skip?

suresh: short summary from the local eval set (task: LQA dev subset, 1k prompts):
```
baseline fp16  : ppl 12.4 | exact_match 0.812
awq (no rescue): ppl 13.2 | exact_match 0.798 (delta -1.7%)
awq + channel-scale on flagged: ppl 12.6 | exact_match 0.807 (delta -0.5%)
awq + skip-layers (keep fp16 for flagged): ppl 12.5 | exact_match 0.809 (delta -0.3%)
gptq fallback on flagged: ppl 12.45 | exact_match 0.810 (delta -0.2%)
```

maya: these numbers suggest channel-scaling is cheap and recovers most of the loss; skip-layer is slightly better but increases memory. GPTQ per-layer is best for accuracy but increases conversion complexity/size.

quant-bot: scan run complete — saved artifact to s3://redwood-experiments/gptish7b/outlier_scan/1769801120.json :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: created issue #2347: "per-layer-gptq-fallback + rescue policy" and linked the scan artifact.

anna: next steps?

suresh: plan: (1) implement per-layer override in converter (elliot), (2) add channel-scaling transform + quick re-eval (maya/suresh), (3) add rescue flags to model profile schema and console UI (product/eng), (4) include fallback routing in serving (eng-runtime). Rolling to dev cluster as an experiment first, then canary.

elliot: I'll open a PR for converter patch with test vectors. ETA EOD tomorrow.

maya: I'll run a more extensive eval (SQuAD-like + multi-turn) and post numbers here.

suresh: thanks — labeling this thread: per-layer-rescue + bakeoff notes. tagging @anna for prioritization. :rocket:
